notes: SUMMARY: ThrottleGuard builds an automated contact center layer for mid-market telco and fintech support teams. Heavy focus on deflection via high-quality bot-first chat and fast agent-assist when escalation required.

Volume profile: ~12M messages/month (inbound user messages), peak concurrency ~9k live chats during product incidents. Typical median session length 8 messages, 95% of sessions < 40 tokens generated per reply (short form).
Primary objective: reduce live agent load by 55-65% while keeping CSAT >= 4.5. Cost sensitivity high — target unit cost < $0.0008 per generated token equivalent in steady state.

Key technical targets: p95 latency < 250ms for assistant suggestions (agent-assist), throughput sustainable for back-to-back spike to 10k concurrent chats for 10 minutes, deterministic fallbacks to smaller/quantized models under load.
Model preferences: prefer open-weights family (quantization-friendly) but will consider Redwood-verified variants; want transparent per-model unit economics and recommended quantization profiles.

Caching/batching needs: strong interest in prefix/KV caching for repeat question patterns, request-aware batching that preserves low-latency SLOs for agent-assist. Looking for suggested batching configs and estimated cost savings.

Security & compliance: SSO via SAML, SOC2 required, encryption keys via KMS, audit logging for token-level access, retention controls (90 days for transcripts), US data residency for regulated telco customers.

POC scope proposed: 2 weeks on Dedicated (4x A100 equiv), run synthetic spike test + 72h steady traffic, evaluate cost per successful deflection, latency SLOs, model quantization A/B test (fp16 vs int8/4), and tooling integration (tool-calling to CRM).
